chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Sam Woodyard, the greatest Ellington drummer
summary: Woodyard had Greer's color plus swing and memory, and could hawk a soloist to death as at Newport '56.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Then Dave stayed for a while and after Dave left then is when Sam Woodyard come in.
To me Sam Woodyard was the greatest drummer that Duke has ever had.

He had everything Greer had plus the swing and a memory. He could paint pictures. He knew exactly how to taste Ellington's arrangements without Duke telling him anything. Sam knew exactly what to do, and he would lay down a rhythm behind you, a beat behind you, forget it. Forget it.
I remember the rhythm section used to say, 'He's a good hawker. He'd just hawk you right to death.'
That's right, he would. He would. If you don't believe it, listen to Newport '56. He hawked poor Paul to death all the way through them 27 choruses.
We didn't -- Did we mention -- Well, we do want to mention Paul --
-- when we get into the Duke Ellington era.
